 is initially 
released as ammonia, and because ammonia is toxic, the liver transforms it into urea. Urea is then 
transported to the kidneys and excreted in the urine. Urea is a molecule that contains two nitrogens 
and is highly soluble in water. This makes it ideal for transporting excess nitrogen out of the body. 
Because amino acids are building blocks that the body reserves in order to synthesize other 
proteins, more than 90 percent of the protein ingested does not get broken down further than the 
amino acid monomers.
